title: Review-qualified goal closure
description: Objective: close J1's remaining evidence-authority gap: goal.close currently trusts opaque caller-supplied verification/review witness refs. Deliverable: a daemon prerequisite composer that reads the exact durable EvidenceReceipt and ReviewOutputAccepted records for the candidate/result, binds their hashes and zero-authority proof into the core closure witness, and only then invokes the existing goal reducer/commit path. NOT in scope: new core rules, review-round persistence, verifier execution, UI, or canary tests. Depends on Durable verification receipt dispatch and the landed review persistence task task-9011e3b32c414e9ca0d49f49fdfaaf08. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-services.ts, goal-services.test.ts, a focused goal-qualification.ts module, and apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts refusal vocabulary if required. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: goal.close derives its verification, review, result, and zero-authority witnesses from matching durable production records; request payload refs/truth labels alone cannot satisfy closure.

Missing receipt, non-passing/UNKNOWN receipt, mismatched result hash, absent ReviewOutputAccepted, stale review package, or remaining authority each refuse with a distinct stable daemon-prerequisite code/layer and commit nothing.
A fully matching verified/reviewed result closes the goal through the existing core reducer in the third J1 human action; no extra human command is introduced.
Replay is idempotent with one durable closure row, and earlier review/evidence records remain readable and byte-identical.
Focused daemon and repo typecheck gates exit 0; the worker mutation-drills the durable read rather than a request-field check.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, evidence half. Write `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-qualification.test.ts` RED against the not-yet-written `qualifyGoalClosure(store, projectId, goalId)`. One case per durable state, each pinning the EXACT code AND that the refusing layer is `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, and each re-reading the store to assert the goal aggregate did not move and `decisionCount` did not grow: (1) approved node in scope with no `FoundationVerificationReceipted` row naming it -> RECEIPT_ABSENT; (2) two receipts whose `receipt.graphIdentity` is the same node -> RECEIPT_AMBIGUOUS; (3) a receipt whose durable bytes were tampered after the fact via `commitRaw`-style direct write so the re-encode byte-compare in `readStoredReceipt` fails -> RECEIPT_UNREADABLE; (4) a receipt read back with verdict FAILED -> NOT_PASSED; (5) the attempt record mutated after verification so `readFoundationAttemptRecord(store, row.attemptAggregateId).digest !== row.recordDigest` -> RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Cases 1-5 must be distinguishable from each other, not merely all-refused: assert the code, since a single earlier guard answering for all five would otherwise pass (see `mem:refusal-test-answered-by-earlier-guard`). If the arms are written as a swept table, assert the generated case count is 5 and > 0.
implementationPlan.note: goal-qualification.test.ts holds the 5 evidence arms, each pinning the exact code AND layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, each snapshotting the store and re-reading goal aggregate + decisionCount + goal event count afterwards. Every arm seeds everything else valid so no earlier guard can answer: ABSENT seeds review acceptance for BOTH nodes and verifies only one; AMBIGUOUS drives two REAL verifications of one node; UNREADABLE plants the same receipt re-serialised non-canonically under its own verification id (only the byte compare in readStoredReceipt can catch it); NOT_PASSED runs a real verifier exiting 3; RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH appends a second RECORDED event so the record no longer reads back. Written as five separate cases, not a sweep, so no generated-count assertion applies. RED confirmed: "Cannot find module './goal-qualification.js'", Test Files 1 failed.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, review + authority half + the positive arm, same test file. (6) node verified but `readReviewLedger(store, projectId, nodeRef).accepted === undefined` -> REVIEW_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED (the existing code, unchanged behaviour); (7) accepted, but `readVerifierReceipt(store, projectId, accepted.verifierReceiptId)` no longer reads back with `accepted.verifierReceiptSha256`, and separately a case where the latest review round's `reviewInputDigest` differs from the accepted one -> REVIEW_PACKAGE_STALE for both, and assert BOTH sub-cases individually (one code, two guards, so the message or the seeded condition must discriminate — see `mem:gotcha-one-code-many-guards-needs-the-message-as-discriminator`); (8) a SECOND `EffectActivationCommitted` on an attempt aggregate whose attempt record carries a `nodeKey` in scope but which no accepted receipt names -> AUTHORITY_REMAINS; (9) an activation on the receipt's own attempt aggregate whose bytes do not read back through `readFoundationActivationHistory` -> AUTHORITY_REMAINS (unreadable authority is not zero authority; fail closed). POSITIVE ARM, and it is load-bearing because a refusal-only suite is blind to a wrong accepted value (`mem:refusal-only-suite-cannot-see-a-wrong-accepted-value`): a fully verified + accepted node yields `ok`, and the test RECOMPUTES the expected `acceptanceClosureRef`, `completionNodeAcceptedRef`, `obligationsHoldRef` and `zeroAuthorityProofRef` from the durable bytes it seeded and asserts equality field by field, plus `truthClass === "DAEMON_VERIFIED"` on both witnesses. Do not recompute by calling the production derivation helper — hash the seeded values independently, or the assertion is a tautology.
implementationPlan.note: Added arms 6-9 plus the positive arm. DEVIATION, measured and forced: the step text's second REVIEW_PACKAGE_STALE sub-case ("latest round's reviewInputDigest differs from the accepted one") is not a real condition - review-acceptance.ts:120,127 records the VERIFIER RECEIPT's reviewInputDigest, which is structurally never a round's (recordVerifierReceipt swaps the DAEMON_RECEIPT package item, verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:197-228), so that comparison would refuse every closure. The honest durable equivalent is used instead: the accepted verifier receipt's source must still be the LATEST review round, the exact comparison acceptOutput itself made at acceptance time. Both stale sub-cases and both authority sub-cases share one code, so each pins the EXACT message via expectRefusedExactly. Positive arm recomputes all four refs by restating the length-framed hash scheme by hand (only the version tag is imported).

implementationPlan.description: Implement `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-qualification.ts` plus its one-line bridge `goal-qualification.js` (`export * from "./goal-qualification.ts";` — every sibling has one and it is git-tracked; without it the module is invisible at runtime). `qualifyGoalClosure(store, projectId, goalId)` returns either `{ok:true, closureWitness, zeroAuthorityWitness}` or `{ok:false, code}`. Algorithm, every input from durable bytes: (a) `readApprovedNodeScope` (step 1) for the node set, null -> REVIEW_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED, unchanged; (b) index the durable receipts by scanning `store.readEventsByTypeAfter(FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_EVENT_TYPES.RECEIPTED, 0n, page)`, take only `verificationId` from each scanned payload and then RE-READ every row through `readStoredReceipt(store, verificationId)` from `../evidence/foundation-verification-store.js` — the scanned bytes are never trusted directly, because `readStoredReceipt` is the only path that re-encodes and byte-compares; key the index by `row.receipt.graphIdentity`, and a second row for one node sets AMBIGUOUS; (c) per node in sorted order run the five evidence checks, then the review checks against `readReviewLedger` + `readVerifierReceipt`; (d) authority: for every `EffectActivationCommitted` event, resolve its aggregate through `readFoundationAttemptRecord` to a `nodeKey`; if that nodeKey is in scope and the aggregate is not the one the node's PASSED receipt names, or `readFoundationActivationHistory` does not read it back with `lease.leaseId === receipt.leaseIdentity` and `effectIntent.intentId === receipt.effectIdentity`, refuse AUTHORITY_REMAINS; (e) derive the witnesses as sha256 over version-tagged ordered tuples of the durable values only (`acceptanceClosureRef` over (nodeRef, receiptSha256, verifierReceiptSha256, reviewInputDigest) plus the approvalRef; `completionNodeAcceptedRef` over the whole ordered accepted node set — design 278's designated completionNodeKey is NOT durable anywhere (grepped: only a test literal), so binding the full approved closure proves more, not less, and this is recorded as a known gap; `obligationsHoldRef` over the receipts' `obligations`; `zeroAuthorityProofRef` over the ordered (leaseIdentity, effectIdentity) pairs and the count of activations scanned), each with `truthClass: "DAEMON_VERIFIED"`. Target <=250 physical lines; if it crosses, split the durable readers into `goal-qualification-reads.ts` with its own `.js` bridge rather than letting one file grow past 400.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
TWO FORKS WERE PUT TO THE HUMAN IN THE REPL AND BOTH WERE DECIDED; do not re-open them.

FORK 1 - what happens to the payload witnesses. Considered (a) derive-and-replace and (b) declare-and-cross-check (the `expectedRecordDigest` / CANDIDATE_STALE pattern from foundation-verification-contracts.ts:146). HUMAN CHOSE (a): the composer derives both witnesses from durable bytes and hands THOSE to `reduceGoal`; the payload keys stay required at ingress for wire compatibility and are inert. (b) was rejected because it needs a seventh payload-mismatch code that DoD 2 does not enumerate, and because every fixture would have to compute derived hashes. The inert-field smell is answered by a test in both directions, not by a comment: garbage payload refs + real durable records -> CLOSES; perfect payload refs + no durable records -> REFUSES.

FORK 2 - what 'remaining authority' means. Design line 278 demands proof of zero live planning/execution/review/qualification leases, attempts, processes, effects, resources, provider slots, funding holds, fences and reconciliation items. NONE of those has a durable terminal record: the activation ledger writes `EffectActivationCommitted` plus exactly three transitions (GRANT_CONSUMED, PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED, PROCESS_OBSERVED) and no release event exists anywhere in apps/daemon, and `LeaseRecord.state` is frozen at ACTIVE by event immutability so it carries no liveness signal. Considered reporting blocked for a prerequisite that lands release records. HUMAN CHOSE the accounted-for-activations measure: every durable activation whose attempt record carries a `nodeKey` in the approved scope must be named by that node's PASSED evidence receipt (`leaseIdentity`, `effectIdentity`); anything unaccounted or unreadable refuses. It is an honest subset of design 278, measurable on committed bytes today, and it fails closed.

planningNotes.risks:
1. BIGGEST RISK - THE FIXTURE, NOT THE COMPOSER. Seeding one durable `FoundationVerificationReceipted` row needs the whole real chain: seedReadyProject -> activation ingress -> launcher authority -> recordProvenFoundationAttempt -> sealRecipe -> verify() spawning a REAL node child. Model it on apps/daemon/src/evidence/foundation-verification-service.test.ts:1-70; do not shortcut it with a recording launcher, because a receipt minted from a fake process is the mock-backed acceptance the rails forbid. Budget step 2 accordingly; if the chain will not seed, report blocked rather than narrowing the DoD.
2. `runVerifierProcess` keeps a MODULE-LEVEL run registry keyed by grantId (documented at foundation-verification-service.test.ts:66-68). Two seeded nodes sharing an effect intent share a grant and the second adopts the first one's run. Derive each seeded node's intent from its nodeRef.
3. The two harnesses both use PROJECT_ID "project-1" (bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:35 and recovery/restore-test-harness.ts:32) so they share one store - convenient, and also the reason a seeding call can collide with the goal aggregate version the close envelope hardcodes (`envelope("goal.close", 2, ...)`, bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:343). Verify the version rather than assuming the fixture writes only to other aggregates.
4. `completionNodeAcceptedRef` HAS NO DURABLE SOURCE. Grep finds `completionNode` only as a test literal at bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:269 and in the core type. Deriving it over the whole approved node set is the deliberate conservative choice; say so in a comment, and do not quietly pick scope[0] or the last element.
5. `exact()` in goal-validation.ts rejects EXTRA keys. A derived witness carrying a helpful debug field fails `validClosure` and the core refuses with a code that looks nothing like the real cause.
6. Mutation drills run in a SHARED worktree (`mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree`): a peer's task-completion hook can commit a whole tree and swallow the drill so git reads clean. Snapshot the file hash before each drill and restore by content, not by `git checkout`.
7. Vitest workers die on a held SQLite handle - every seeded store must go through the harness `closeStores` in `afterEach`.
8. A refusal test whose seeded condition is answered by an EARLIER guard passes while testing nothing. The five evidence arms in step 3 sit behind each other in one loop; assert the exact code per arm and, for the two REVIEW_PACKAGE_STALE guards sharing one code, make the seeded condition itself the discriminator.
9. Per-file cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE. goal-qualification.ts is the one at risk; the split into goal-qualification-reads.ts is pre-authorised in step 5 and both halves need a .js bridge.
